proved_step: For any finite graph G=(V,L⊔R), let M have rows indexed by X⊆L and columns by Y⊆R, with M[X,Y]=1 iff X∪Y is a perfect matching. Let B be the vertices incident to at least one edge of L and at least one edge of R. Over every field, rank(M)≤2^{|B|}. Proof: A row indexed by X is zero unless X is a matching and covers every vertex incident only to L; likewise a column Y is zero unless Y is a matching and covers every vertex incident only to R. For nonzero rows and columns, X∪Y is a perfect matching exactly when the subsets of B covered by X and Y are disjoint and have union B. Thus compatibility depends only on the subset of B covered by X. Any two nonzero rows whose X cover the same subset of B agree on every column; zero rows also contribute no rank. There are at most 2^{|B|} distinct nonzero rows, so the row rank, hence the rank, is at most 2^{|B|}. This does not establish a lower bound for perfect matching or close a Route F obligation.

statement_start: For every finite simple graph G=(V,E), the satisfying assignments of Phi_G = AND_{uv in E} EXACT1(x_u,x_v,z_uv) project onto exactly the independent sets of G, and each projected assignment has a unique extension to the z variables.
statement: For every finite simple graph G=(V,E), the satisfying assignments of Phi_G = AND_{uv in E} EXACT1(x_u,x_v,z_uv) project onto exactly the independent sets of G, and each projected assignment has a unique extension to the z variables. Proof: Fix an assignment x to V. For an edge uv, the equation x_u+x_v+z_uv=1 with all variables Boolean has a solution z_uv iff x_u+x_v<=1, equivalently not both endpoints are selected. When it has a solution, it is uniquely z_uv=1-x_u-x_v. Thus a satisfying extension exists iff x is an independent set, and then all auxiliary values are uniquely determined edge by edge. This also covers E empty, where every x is independent and there is exactly one empty assignment to z. Hence the projection is precisely the independent-set family and is bijective on extensions. This repairs the encoding boundary only; it does not establish any d-SDNNF lower bound or circuit lower bound.
